column3: The Hebrew calls the Israelites “sons of Israel.”
The Hebrew literally calls the LORD “a man of war.”
The Hebrew name for the sea is “Sea of Reeds.”
The Hebrew compares the standing currents to a heap or mound, rather than explicitly a wall.
The Hebrew preserves “my soul” and describes the hand dispossessing them.
The Hebrew describes being fearsome in praises, rather than simply revered.
The Hebrew verbs describe having led the redeemed people, rather than future leading.
The Hebrew begins “peoples have heard,” rather than “will hear.”
The Hebrew describes the chiefs’ terror and the inhabitants’ melting with completed verb forms, rather than uniformly future actions.
The Hebrew names the “Sea of Reeds,” rendered “Red Sea.”
The Hebrew says “a tree” or “wood,” rendered “a log,” and does not repeat Moses’ name.
The Hebrew says the diseases were placed on “Egypt,” rather than specifically “the Egyptians.”
